items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: I heard him in the band concert in Washington, D. C. ... And he didn't play -- he couldn't play any jazz. ... I liked what he was doing, you know. He could play.

ctx.x: But, you know, back in those days when I came along, it isn't like today where kids, they learn about tone -- intonation and all this before they even get the instruments they learn. There was no road to go on. We had to make our own road for the kids, you know, today, back there in those days. Really because all a trombone player did back then was -- (imitates a trombone). That's the only way they played. They didn't know any other way to play.

In fact, the first trombone player I ever heard in my life that didn't play like that was a guy called I think it was Arthur Prior. He was a band -- it wasn't a jazz band -- he was a band master, you know. And he played all these intricate parts in a band. And I said, wow, I sure want to play like that, you know. And I don't want to play all this
